newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASC seeks fairer presentation of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASC seeks fairer presentation of forecasts.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Thursday it hoped to provide greater protection for investors by encouraging fairer presentation of financial forecasts in prospectuses.

"The ASC recognises that financial forecasts in prospectuses can be a useful source of information about a company's prospects, but it is concerned about investors' possible over-reliance on these forecasts," the regulator said in releasing a discussion paper on the issue.
The ASC said that if financial forecasts are included in prospectuses, they must tell investors about significant uncertainties in the forecasts.

"The ASC believes investors don't get enough information about the basis of the some forecasts nor are they always told of all the material risks that the forecast results may not occur," the commission said.
"The significant level of failure of companies to meet forecasts mean investors need to read forecasts critically and find out if they are based on reasonable assumptions," it said.

The discussion papers include draft guidelines designed to help directors and experts avoid making misleading forecasts, give enough information to allow investors to make a reasonable assessment, and to give guidance on how the ASC will enforce prospectus disclosure requirements in relation to forecasts.

The papers contain a review of overseas approaches to regulation of forecasts and seek comment on whether, if there is a reasonable basis for a profit forecast in a share prospectus, it is information that investors reasonably require and would reasonably expect to find in the prospectus.
The ASC said it would review its position after considering comments from industry and investors.
In the meantime, it said it would continue to check prospectuses that contain profit forecasts to see that they are soundly based on disclosed assumptions and fairly presented.
